13: We roll two symmetric six-sided dice n times. Find all n for which the probability of getting the same number on both dice at least once is less than 671/1296. [Card value is the sum of all valid n.]
14: Compute the limit, as n tends to infinity, of [1+4+7+...+(3n-2)] divided by [5+7+9+...+(2n+3)].
18: The pairs (x,y) satisfying the system of equations {-4x^2+y^2+2y+1=0; -x^2+y+4=0} are the coordinates of the vertices of a convex quadrilateral ABCD. a) Find the coordinates of points A, B, C, D. b) Show that ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid. c) Find the equation of the circle circumscribed on ABCD. [Card value sums only the numeric part a: x_A+y_A+x_B+y_B+x_C+y_C+x_D+y_D; parts b and c are excluded as proof/expression.]
19: Given the equation $x^2+(m-5)x+m^2+m+ rac{1}{4}=0$. Investigate for which values of the parameter $m$ the ratio of the sum of the real roots of the equation to their product attains its smallest value. Find this value. [Card value is $m$ + the smallest value.]
